phase1.intro:
ListView and TableView are the storefront's catalog board — showing a whole collection at once.

Where should we start?

topics.buttonText: Why do these controls need an ObservableList instead of a plain one?
dialogue: Both are backed by an [[term:ObservableList]] (`FXCollections.observableArrayList(...)`), not a plain ArrayList. [[key:That's the entire trick behind these controls staying in sync with your data]]: call `listView.setItems(observableList)` once, and add()/remove() calls automatically update what's rendered.

stickyNote.flavor: 📡 broadcasts its own changes to the view
stickyNote.definition: ListView/TableView are backed by an ObservableList — add()/remove() on it automatically update the rendered view, no manual refresh needed.

topics.buttonText: What's the difference between ListView and TableView?
dialogue: ListView<T> is the simple version: one column, rendered with each item's toString() by default. TableView<T> is the structured version: multiple named columns, each wired to a property of T via [[term:PropertyValueFactory]] — `new PropertyValueFactory<>("name")` calls [[key:getName() on each row's object]], matched by naming convention.

stickyNote.flavor: 📋 one column vs. many named, property-backed columns
stickyNote.definition: ListView shows one column via toString(). TableView shows multiple named columns, each backed by a PropertyValueFactory matching a getter by naming convention.

topics.buttonText: What happens if I typo the property name?
dialogue: [[warn:PropertyValueFactory's string has to match the property name exactly]] — "name" looks for getName(), and a typo there fails the same silent way FXML's fx:id mismatch does: no compile error, just an empty column.

stickyNote.flavor: 🔇 a typo fails silently — empty column, no error
stickyNote.definition: A mismatched PropertyValueFactory string (not matching a getter's name exactly) fails silently — no compile error, just an empty column.

phase1.output: (Window with ListView showing items, TableView showing people, with add/remove controls)
phase1.openingDialogue: ListView and TableView stay in sync automatically because they're backed by an ObservableList — no manual refresh required. 📡

phase2.errorMessage: (TableView appears with header but NO DATA and blank columns!)
phase2.explanation:
[[warn:the table renders — headers, borders, everything — but every cell is blank]].

The columns exist, and the ObservableList of data exists, but [[key:each TableColumn was never told which property to pull from each row]] — that's the job of setCellValueFactory(new PropertyValueFactory<>("propertyName")), and it's missing here. Without it, a TableColumn has perfectly good headers and perfectly good rows to iterate over, but no instructions for what to actually display inside each cell, so it defaults to showing nothing.

phase3.openingDialogue: ListView and TableView — display your data! 📋

mcq.question:
A TableView<Person> column is set up with new PropertyValueFactory<>("age"), but the Person class only has a method called getAgeInYears() — no getAge(). What happens?

A) A compile error, since PropertyValueFactory checks method names at compile time
B) It falls back to calling toString() on the whole Person object
C) The column renders with every cell blank — no matching getAge() is found at runtime
D) It throws a NoSuchMethodException that crashes the app immediately on launch

phase4.selfChallenge:
Write a JavaFX program with:
1. A ListView<String> of programming languages: "Java", "Python", "C++", "JavaScript"
2. A TextField and Button to add new languages
3. A Button to remove the selected language
4. A Label that shows the selected language when clicked

Use ObservableList for the ListView data.

phase5.trivia: [[fun:PropertyValueFactory finds its getter through reflection]] — the string "name" is turned into a search for a method named exactly getName() (or a JavaBean-style nameProperty()) on your row object, matched purely by that naming convention. It's the same reflection-by-convention trick FXMLLoader used back in 5.9 to match fx:id strings to controller fields.
